traveler: Ezekiel son of Buzi (Yehezqel ben Buzi), priest and prophet of the exile
title: The River Chebar: the Priest Deported, the Chariot Seen, the House Measured
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: From the Priests' Court to the Land of the Chaldeans

stops.name: Jerusalem, the Temple Mount: the son of Buzi
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. No source gives a birth year. The figure c. 623 BC is derived by reading 'the thirtieth year' of Ezekiel 1:1 as the prophet's age at his call in 593 BC, which is only one of several readings; others take it as a Babylonian or jubilee reckoning. The priestly descent from Buzi is attested at Ezekiel 1:3; the date is not
stops.campa: A son is born to Buzi the priest in the years when Josiah is scouring the high places out of Judah and the book of the law has just been found in the house. The boy is a kohen by birth, entered on the rolls of the men who serve the altar, and everything he is taught is measured: the courses of the priests, the cubits of the courts, what may be eaten, what may be touched, which gate faces east. He is trained for a house that stands. Nothing in that training allows for the house being carried away.
stops.quote: The word of the Lord came expressly unto Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Chebar; and the hand of the Lord was there upon him.
suggested_refs: The priestly courses of the First Temple, the world Ezekiel was trained into

stops.name: Jerusalem, the City of David: Jehoiachin goes out to the king of Babylon
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. The Babylonian Chronicle gives 2 Adar of Nebuchadnezzar's seventh year, converting to 16 March 597 BC; 2 Kings 24:10-16 narrates the surrender and the deportation without a date
stops.campa: Nebuchadnezzar's army stands at the wall and the boy king Jehoiachin walks out to it after three months on the throne. The city is not burned. It is emptied instead of everything portable: the king, the queen mother, the officers, the smiths and the armourers, the gold vessels cut up out of the treasuries, and ten thousand of the leading men with the priests among them. Ezekiel goes in this first column, a man of the Temple taken away from the Temple while the daily offering still smokes behind him.
suggested_refs: The Babylonian Chronicle tablet ABC 5, recording the taking of the city of Judah

stops.name: Riblah on the Orontes, the column counted at the forward camp
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. No ancient text places Ezekiel or the 597 BC column at Riblah. Riblah is attested as Nebuchadnezzar's western headquarters for the related deportation of 587/586 BC (2 Kings 25:6-7, 20-21), and the routing of the earlier column past it is inferred from Babylonian logistics alone
stops.campa: The road out of Judah runs north before it runs east, because the desert cannot be crossed straight. At Riblah on the Orontes the Babylonian command keeps its forward camp, where officers muster, provision, and count what the western campaign has taken. Eleven years on, the last king of Judah will be brought to this same camp to watch his sons killed and then be blinded, so that the killing is the last thing his eyes hold. The column of 597 passes the tents and keeps walking, most of the distance still in front of it.
suggested_refs: Riblah in the land of Hamath, Nebuchadnezzar's standing headquarters for the western wars
sources: route reconstruction from Neo-Babylonian campaign logistics

stops.name: Damascus, the deportation road through the orchards
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. No source names Damascus in connection with Ezekiel or with the 597 BC deportees. The leg is inferred from the standard Levant-to-Babylonia caravan route
stops.campa: The road bends through Damascus, the oldest watered city on the way, its orchards fed by the Barada and its markets stocked from every direction at once. The exiles are walking through the ordinary business of an empire that has just eaten their country: grain moving, taxes moving, other men's gods carried in other men's carts. Ezekiel is a priest without an altar, in a place where every altar belongs to someone else. Ahead of them the green ends and the caravan tracks turn east into stone and gravel.
suggested_refs: The Damascus oasis on the Barada, obligatory stage of the northern route east
sources: route reconstruction from regional caravan geography; not attested for Ezekiel

stops.name: Tadmor, the oasis in the middle of the waste
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. Tadmor is not named in any source concerning Ezekiel or the 597 BC column; it is included as the standard water stop on the Syrian desert crossing
stops.campa: Between the Syrian steppe and the Euphrates there is one reliable water, and the caravans have used it since long before there is a name for the empire that owns it. At Tadmor the springs come up sulphurous and warm under the palms, and the column drinks and is counted again. From here there is nothing to look at for days but a horizon with no hill in it. The man walking in it was raised inside a walled city on a ridge, in a house of courts inside courts, where nothing was ever more than a wall away.
suggested_refs: The Efqa spring at Tadmor, water of the desert crossing
sources: route reconstruction from caravan geography; not attested for Ezekiel

stops.name: Circesium, the Euphrates reached at the mouth of the Khabur
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. Not attested for Ezekiel. Coordinates corrected in this file to 35.1558 / 40.4300, the confluence site of modern al-Busayra; the figure of 34.4667 / 40.9167 carried in the source pool is roughly 90 km wrong and falls in open desert downstream
stops.campa: The desert track ends where the Khabur comes down out of the north and empties into the Euphrates, and from that junction the great river runs south all the way to Babylonia. The exiles come off gravel onto mud. There is reed and tamarisk, there are fishermen, there are boats going the direction they are going. Everything from here is water and canal and flat black soil, a country that grows by being cut into channels. Ezekiel will spend the rest of his life beside one of those channels.
suggested_refs: The Khabur-Euphrates confluence at Circesium, modern al-Busayra
sources: route reconstruction; not attested for Ezekiel

stops.name: Mari, downstream past the buried mound
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. Not attested for Ezekiel. Ordered here after Circesium because Mari lies downstream of the Khabur mouth; the source pool listed the two waypoints in the reverse order, which would run the column back up the river
stops.campa: Below the confluence the river passes a long mound on the west bank where a city ruled this whole reach of the Euphrates a thousand years before any of these people were born, and was burned, and was never rebuilt. It had a palace, an archive, a treasury and gods of its own, and men who kept its rolls in a script nobody in this column can read. The exiles walk past the heap of it without a name they would recognise, and nobody stops to ask whose capital it was.
suggested_refs: Tell Hariri, the mound of Mari on the middle Euphrates
sources: route reconstruction from Euphrates caravan geography; not attested for Ezekiel

stops.name: Babylon, the destination of the deportation
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction as to Ezekiel's own presence. Babylon is attested as the destination of the 597 BC deportation (2 Kings 24:15); the Book of Ezekiel never places him inside the capital, giving his residence consistently as Tel Abib by the Chebar
stops.campa: The city the column has been walked toward for five months is bigger than anything in Judah: the processional way, the glazed beasts on the Ishtar Gate, the ziggurat, the temple of Marduk, the ration tablets in the palace storerooms where a scribe enters oil and barley for Yaukin, king of the land of Yahud, and his sons. Jehoiachin is kept here. Ezekiel is not. The priests and the craftsmen are settled out in the canal country to work land the empire wants worked, and that is where the word will find him.
suggested_refs: The Babylon ration tablets recording oil and barley for Yaukin of Yahud and his five sons

stops.name: The Chebar canal near Nippur, the heavens opened
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day in the text, which gives the fourth month, fifth day, and fixes the year as the fifth of Jehoiachin's exile (Ezekiel 1:2); the conversion to 31 July 593 BC follows the standard Babylonian tables. The meaning of the parallel phrase 'the thirtieth year' is disputed and unresolved
stops.campa: Five years into the exile, on a working canal cut for irrigation, among people digging and hauling for the empire that brought them, the sky comes apart. A storm wind out of the north, a great cloud, fire folding in on itself, and brightness around it. The Chebar is not a holy place. It is an engineering work in a flat country, cut to move water onto fields, and the priest standing on its bank is five hundred miles from the only altar he is permitted to serve. The heavens open over the irrigation ditch.
stops.quote: Now it came to pass in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, in the fifth day of the month, as I was among the captives by the river of Chebar, that the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God.
suggested_refs: The nar Kabari, the great canal past Nippur, named in the Murashu tablets

stops.name: The Chebar canal, the wheels and the throne of sapphire
stops.date_confidence: attested; same date formula as Ezekiel 1:1
stops.campa: Out of the fire come four living creatures with the likeness of a man, each with four faces and four wings, feet like a calf's hoof, burnished bronze, moving straight forward and never turning as they go. Beside each is a wheel, and a wheel within the wheel, and the rims are high and full of eyes. Over their heads a firmament like terrible crystal, and above it a throne of sapphire, and on the throne the appearance of a man, fire from the loins upward and fire from the loins downward, with a rainbow standing round about.
stops.quote: As the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud in the day of rain, so was the appearance of the brightness round about. This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the Lord. And when I saw it, I fell upon my face, and I heard a voice of one that spake.
suggested_refs: The merkabah of Ezekiel 1, source of the four living creatures and the wheels within wheels

stops.name: The Chebar canal, the scroll that tastes of honey
stops.date_confidence: attested to the vision unit; the text gives no separate date formula between Ezekiel 1:1 and 8:1
stops.campa: The voice calls him son of man and stands him on his feet, and sends him to a house of rebels with hard faces and stiff hearts, whether they hear or whether they forbear. A hand is put out holding a roll of a book, written within and without with lamentations and mourning and woe, and he is told to eat it. He eats, and in his mouth it is sweet as honey. He is given a forehead harder than theirs, adamant harder than flint, and a commission: he is a watchman, and the blood of the unwarned will be required at his hand.
suggested_refs: The eaten scroll of Ezekiel 2:8-3:3, taken up again in Revelation 10

stops.name: Tel Abib, seven days sitting among them
stops.date_confidence: attested to the interval of seven days (Ezekiel 3:15); the absolute date is calculated forward from the call vision
stops.campa: The spirit lifts him and takes him away, and he goes in bitterness, in the heat of his spirit, with the hand of the Lord strong upon him. He comes to the deportees settled at Tel Abib on the Chebar and sits down where they sit, and stays there seven days, astonished, saying nothing. They are Judeans put on the land to farm canal country, keeping their genealogies and their sabbaths where there is no house to bring either to. The word does not come again until the week is out.
suggested_refs: Tel Abib, an unidentified tell on the Kebar canal, known only from the Book of Ezekiel

stops.name: Tel Abib, the watchman with his tongue bound
stops.date_confidence: attested to the vision unit, undated in the text; placed immediately after the seven days of Ezekiel 3:15
stops.campa: He is made watchman over the house of Israel: if the sword comes and the watchman gave no warning, the dead man dies in his sin but the blood is on the watchman. Then he is shut in his house, bound with cords, and his tongue is made to cleave to the roof of his mouth so that he is dumb, opened only when there is a word to deliver and closed again after it. For the next eight years the warnings are delivered by his body instead: a brick, a rope, a razor, a bundle carried out through a wall at dusk.
suggested_refs: The watchman charge of Ezekiel 3:16-21, repeated at Ezekiel 33

stops.name: Tel Abib, the city drawn on a brick
stops.date_confidence: undated in the text; placed shortly after the call vision of 593 BC on the order of the chapters
stops.campa: He takes a clay tile, the ordinary writing material of the country he has been brought to, and draws Jerusalem on it. Then he builds a siege against the drawing: a fort, a ramp, camps, battering rams set round about, and an iron plate stood upright between his own face and the city as a wall of separation. He does this in the open, where the settlement can watch him do it. The exiles at Tel Abib are still being told by other men that the deportation is temporary and the city will hold.
stops.quote: Thou also, son of man, take thee a tile, and lay it before thee, and pourtray upon it the city, even Jerusalem: And lay siege against it, and build a fort against it, and cast a mount against it; set the camp also against it, and set battering rams against it round about.
suggested_refs: Neo-Babylonian clay tiles and city plans, the material of the sign-act

stops.name: Tel Abib, three hundred and ninety days on his left side
stops.date_confidence: undated in the text. The counts of 390 and 40 days are given as measures of iniquity borne, and it is disputed whether they were lived out as a continuous performance or given as a sign in figure only
stops.campa: He is laid on his left side and bound with cords so that he cannot turn, and he bears the iniquity of the house of Israel three hundred and ninety days, a day assigned for each year. Then on his right side forty days for the house of Judah. The face of the man in the dirt is set toward the drawn city and his arm is bared against it. A priest's body is required at the altar unblemished and standing. This one lies in the dirt of a foreign settlement, bound, as a public record of a punishment not yet fallen.
stops.quote: Lie thou also upon thy left side, and lay the iniquity of the house of Israel upon it: according to the number of the days that thou shalt lie upon it thou shalt bear their iniquity.
suggested_refs: The 390 and 40 day counts of Ezekiel 4, and the divergent totals of the Septuagint

stops.name: Tel Abib, bread by weight and water by measure
stops.date_confidence: undated in the text; continuous with the sign-act of Ezekiel 4:4-8
stops.campa: He is told to mix wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet and spelt in one vessel and bake it into bread, twenty shekels a day by weight, and to drink water by measure, a sixth part of a hin, and to bake it in their sight over human dung for fuel. He objects that nothing polluted has entered his mouth from his youth, and he is permitted cow's dung instead. It is the only order in the book he argues with, and he argues with it as a priest. The bread of a siege is being eaten five hundred miles from the siege.
suggested_refs: The mixed-grain famine bread of Ezekiel 4:9, still baked as a devotional recipe

stops.name: Tel Abib, the head shaved with a sword
stops.date_confidence: undated in the text; placed immediately after the sign-acts of Ezekiel 4 on the order of the chapters
stops.campa: He takes a sharp sword and uses it as a barber's razor on his own head and beard, then weighs the hair on balances and divides it in three. A third he burns inside the drawn city when the siege days are finished, a third he strikes with the sword all around it, a third he scatters to the wind. A few hairs he binds in his skirt, and even some of those he throws into the fire. The law forbids a priest to make baldness on his head or to shave the corner of his beard. He does both, in public, with a weapon, and tells them this is what will be done to the people of that drawing.
suggested_refs: The threefold division of the hair, Ezekiel 5:1-4

stops.name: Jerusalem, the Temple: the chambers of imagery
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day: the sixth year, sixth month, fifth day (Ezekiel 8:1), converting to 17 September 592 BC on the standard Babylonian tables. The transport is stated by the text itself to be visionary and not bodily
stops.campa: He is sitting in his house with the elders of Judah in front of him when a hand takes him by a lock of his hair and the spirit lifts him between the earth and the heaven and brings him to Jerusalem. He is shown a hole in a wall, and told to dig, and behind it a door, and behind the door seventy elders of Israel in the dark with censers, every creeping thing and abominable beast painted round the chamber. At the north gate women sit weeping for Tammuz. In the inner court twenty-five men face east and worship the sun.
suggested_refs: The four abominations of Ezekiel 8, seen from Babylonia

stops.name: Jerusalem, the Temple Mount: the glory rises off the threshold
stops.date_confidence: attested; same vision unit as Ezekiel 8:1
stops.campa: Six men come from the upper gate with slaughter weapons in their hands, and with them one in linen with a writer's inkhorn at his side, who is sent through the city to set a mark on the foreheads of those that sigh and cry for its abominations. The rest are cut down, beginning at the sanctuary. While the killing goes on, the glory of the God of Israel lifts off the cherub, moves to the threshold of the house, and stands there; the court fills with brightness; and the wheels are heard to the outer court like the voice of God speaking.
suggested_refs: The man in linen with the inkhorn, Ezekiel 9, and the mark set on the forehead

stops.name: The Mount of Olives, the glory stands east of the city
stops.date_confidence: attested to the vision; Ezekiel 11:23 says only 'the mountain which is on the east side of the city', identified with the Mount of Olives by long convention rather than by the text
stops.campa: The glory goes out from the midst of the city and stands upon the mountain on the east side of it, and stays there, and then the vision goes up from him and he is back in Chaldea among the exiles, telling them what he has seen. The building is still standing and the offerings are still being made in it. The presence it was built to hold has walked out of it eastward, which is the direction the deportees were taken. It does not come back down off that ridge in his lifetime.
suggested_refs: The departure of the shekinah by the east gate, Ezekiel 10:18-11:23

stops.name: Tel Abib, the baggage carried out through the wall
stops.date_confidence: undated in the text; placed between the dated oracles of 592 and 591 BC on the order of the chapters
stops.campa: By daylight, where they can see him, he brings out an exile's bundle, the little a man can carry. At dusk he digs through the mud-brick wall of his own house with his hands and takes the bundle out through the hole with his face covered so that he cannot see the ground. They ask him what he is doing. He tells them it is the prince in Jerusalem, who will go out at twilight through a breach and cover his face, and be taken in a net to Babylon, and never see it though he dies there.
stops.quote: Ezekiel disagreed with him, and said that Zedekiah should not see Babylon ... he was also made blind, and brought to Babylon, but did not see it, according to the prediction of Ezekiel.
stops.quote_source: Josephus, Antiquities of the Jews, Book X (Whiston translation)
suggested_refs: The sign of the exile's baggage, Ezekiel 12:1-16, read against the blinding of Zedekiah
sources: Josephus, Antiquities of the Jews X

stops.name: Tel Abib, the elders sitting before him
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day: the seventh year, fifth month, tenth day (Ezekiel 20:1), converting to 14 August 591 BC
stops.campa: Certain of the elders of Israel come to enquire of the Lord and sit down in front of him, and he is told to refuse them: they have set up their idols in their heart and he will not be enquired of by them. Instead he gives them their own history back, generation by generation, Egypt and the wilderness and the land, a rebellion at every stage. Twice already he has been told that even Noah, Daniel and Job standing together in that country could deliver no one but themselves.
suggested_refs: Ezekiel 14:14 and its Daniel, one of the earliest references to that name outside his own book

stops.name: Tel Abib, the foundling raised to a queen
stops.date_confidence: undated in the text; placed with the oracles of the years between the call and the siege
stops.campa: He tells the city its own life as the life of a woman: a newborn thrown out in a field in her blood, nobody pitying her, and one passing by who says to her, live. She is washed, oiled, clothed in embroidered work and badgers' skin, given bracelets and a chain and a crown, and becomes exceeding beautiful and prospers into a kingdom. Then she trusts in her own beauty and spends it on everyone who passes. The oracle runs sixty-three verses, strips her in front of her lovers, and ends by giving her an everlasting covenant and stopping her mouth in her shame.
suggested_refs: Ezekiel 16, the longest sustained allegory in the prophetic books

stops.name: Tel Abib, the two eagles and the vine
stops.date_confidence: undated in the text; the political situation it describes places it between Zedekiah's Egyptian overture and the start of the siege, roughly 591 to 589 BC
stops.campa: A great eagle with long wings comes to Lebanon, crops off the highest twig of the cedar and carries it to a city of merchants, then takes seed of the land and plants it as a low spreading vine by great waters. The vine turns its roots toward a second eagle. Ezekiel names the treaty under the figure: Nebuchadnezzar took an oath of the king he installed, and the king has broken it and sent to Egypt for horses. He shall die in the midst of Babylon, in the place of the king that made him king, whose oath he despised.
suggested_refs: Ezekiel 17:13-19, the clearest contemporary account of the vassal oath sworn at Riblah

stops.name: Tel Abib, the sour grapes
stops.date_confidence: undated in the text; placed among the oracles of the years before the siege
stops.campa: There is a proverb going around the settlement: the fathers have eaten sour grapes and the children's teeth are set on edge. It is a way of saying that the exile is inherited and nothing any of them does now can matter. He is given an answer to it that takes the whole chapter: all souls are mine, says the Lord, the soul that sinneth, it shall die. The son shall not bear the iniquity of the father. Turn yourselves, and live. He is saying it to men who have already lost the country and have spent a generation being told they lost it for their fathers.
suggested_refs: Ezekiel 18 and the answer to Jeremiah 31:29, the same proverb in two prophets

segments.name: The Siege and the Silence Broken

stops.name: Tel Abib, the day written down
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day in the text, disputed in conversion. Ezekiel 24:1 gives the ninth year, tenth month, tenth day, which converts to 15 January 588 BC by Parker and Dubberstein's reckoning from Jehoiachin's exile, matching 2 Kings 25:1. Wikipedia's article on the siege dates Nebuchadnezzar's investment of the city to January 589 BC, and the pool that fed this file carried both values. The contradiction is recorded, not resolved
stops.campa: He is told to write the name of the day, this same day, because the king of Babylon has set himself against Jerusalem this same day. Nothing has reached the settlement; no runner has come; the siege is five hundred miles away and hours old. Then the parable of the pot: set it on, pour in the water, gather the pieces and the choice bones, let it seethe until the flesh is consumed, then set it empty on the coals until the brass burns and the scum of it is molten. Her scum is in her, and it will not go out.
suggested_refs: The date formula of Ezekiel 24:1-2 set beside 2 Kings 25:1

stops.name: Tel Abib, the desire of his eyes
stops.date_confidence: undated. Ezekiel 24:15 opens a fresh oracle with no date formula of its own; the widespread claim that the wife dies on the day the siege begins is an inference from the chapter's arrangement and is not in the text. The date here is placed shortly after 24:1
stops.campa: He is told in the morning that the desire of his eyes will be taken from him at a stroke, and that he is not to mourn or weep, not to let his tears run down, not to cover his lip, not to eat the bread of men, but to bind his headdress on and put his shoes on his feet and go about as though nothing has happened. He speaks to the people that morning. At evening his wife dies. In the morning he does as he was commanded, and when they ask him what it means to them he tells them: this is your sign.
stops.quote: Son of man, behold, I take away from thee the desire of thine eyes with a stroke: yet neither shalt thou mourn nor weep, neither shall thy tears run down. ... So I spake unto the people in the morning: and at even my wife died; and I did in the morning as I was commanded.
suggested_refs: Ezekiel 24:15-27, the only appearance of the prophet's wife in the book

stops.name: Tel Abib, judgment on the neighbours
stops.date_confidence: undated in the text as a block; the oracles of Ezekiel 25 presuppose the siege and are conventionally placed in its later stages
stops.campa: Ammon said aha against the sanctuary when it was profaned. Moab said the house of Judah is like all the heathen. Edom took vengeance and was greatly guilty. The Philistines took vengeance with a despiteful heart, out of old hatred. Each of the four gets a few lines and a verdict. Ezekiel never goes to any of these countries; they lie behind him along the road he was marched down eleven years ago. He is a deportee in Chaldea pronouncing sentence on states that gloated as his was dismantled.
suggested_refs: The oracles against the nations, Ezekiel 25-32

stops.name: Tel Abib, the great crocodile in the midst of his rivers
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day: the tenth year, tenth month, twelfth day (Ezekiel 29:1), converting to 7 January 587 BC
stops.campa: Egypt is the ally Judah keeps buying and keeps being failed by, a staff of reed that splits in the hand and tears the shoulder that leaned on it. Ezekiel puts Pharaoh in the Nile as the great dragon lying in the midst of his own rivers, saying my river is mine own and I have made it for myself; hooks are put in his jaws and he is dragged up into the open field with the fish of his rivers sticking to his scales. The land is to lie desolate forty years, and afterwards return, and be the basest of the kingdoms.
suggested_refs: Ezekiel 29 and the reed-staff of Egypt at 2 Kings 18:21

stops.name: Jerusalem, the Temple Mount: the house burned
stops.date_confidence: attested to the campaign, disputed as to year. 2 Kings 25:8-9 gives the seventh day of the fifth month of Nebuchadnezzar's nineteenth year; scholarship divides between 587 and 586 BC and this file carries 587 to agree with the date already fixed for Nebuchadnezzar. Ezekiel is not present; he is in Babylonia and does not yet know
stops.campa: Eighteen months into the siege the wall is breached, the king is caught in the plain of Jericho and taken to Riblah, and Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard comes up and burns the house of the Lord and the king's house and every great house in the city. The bronze pillars and the bronze sea are broken up for freight. The platform Ezekiel was born to serve is cleared. In Chaldea the settlement at Tel Abib knows none of this, and the mute man who drew it on a brick eight years ago goes on waiting for news.
suggested_refs: The burning of the First Temple, 2 Kings 25:8-21 and Jeremiah 52

stops.name: Tel Abib, the ship broken in the heart of the seas
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year, incomplete in the text: Ezekiel 26:1 gives the eleventh year and the first day but no month, so the date falls somewhere in 587/586 BC and the month here is a placeholder
stops.campa: Tyre said of Jerusalem, aha, she is broken that was the gates of the people, and Ezekiel answers with the longest single lament in the book. The city is built as a ship: fir of Senir for planks, cedar of Lebanon for a mast, oaks of Bashan for oars, fine linen of Egypt for a sail, the ancients of Gebal as caulkers, and a manifest of every trade from Tarshish to Sheba. Then an east wind breaks her in the midst of the seas, and the merchants of the people hiss at her, and she is never found again.
suggested_refs: The Tyre trade catalogue of Ezekiel 27, the fullest inventory of Iron Age Mediterranean commerce

stops.name: Tel Abib, the fugitive: the city is smitten
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day: the twelfth year, tenth month, fifth day (Ezekiel 33:21), converting to 8 January 585 BC. Some manuscripts read eleventh year, which would shorten the gap. On a 587 fall the news takes about eighteen months to arrive, on a 586 fall about six; the fall year is itself disputed and this file does not resolve it
stops.campa: A man who got out of Jerusalem alive walks into the settlement and says four words: the city is smitten. The evening before he arrived the hand of the Lord had already been on Ezekiel and his mouth had already been opened, so that when the messenger reaches him he is speaking again after years of enforced dumbness. Everything he mimed with his body has now happened. From this day the oracles change direction: no more sieges drawn on bricks, no more hair divided by the sword, but a valley, and a house, and a river.
stops.quote: And it came to pass in the twelfth year of our captivity, in the tenth month, in the fifth day of the month, that one that had escaped out of Jerusalem came unto me, saying, The city is smitten. Now the hand of the Lord was upon me in the evening, afore he that was escaped came; and had opened my mouth, until he came to me in the morning; and my mouth was opened, and I was no more dumb.
suggested_refs: Ezekiel 33:21-22 and the lifting of the dumbness imposed at Ezekiel 3:26

stops.name: The valley of the very dry bones
stops.date_confidence: undated and unplaced. The text names no valley and gives no date formula; the pin is set at Tel Abib because that is where the prophet's body is when the hand of the Lord carries him out in the spirit
stops.campa: He is set down in the middle of a valley full of bones and led round about them, and they are very many and very dry. He is asked whether they can live and answers that only God knows. He prophesies as commanded and there is a noise and a shaking, and bone comes to bone, and sinews and flesh come up on them, and skin covers them, and there is no breath in them. He prophesies to the wind from the four winds, and the breath enters, and they stand up on their feet, an exceeding great army.
stops.quote: The hand of the Lord was upon me, and carried me out in the spirit of the Lord, and set me down in the midst of the valley which was full of bones.
suggested_refs: The Dura-Europos synagogue fresco of the valley of dry bones, third century CE

stops.name: The plain of Dura, the valley as tradition sites it
stops.date_confidence: traditional and undated. No ancient source ties the vision to a named valley; the identification with the plain of Dura south of Babylon, and with the country around al-Kifl, is later Jewish and Islamic folk geography, and the coordinates are approximate
stops.campa: The plain south of Babylon where the book of Daniel sets the golden image and the fiery furnace is the ground that later tradition hands the bones to. Nothing in the prophet's own account puts him here or anywhere; the vision arrives with no name attached to its landscape, no road running to it and none running away. Pilgrims coming to the tomb country on the Euphrates will be shown a plain and told this is the place, and no one is in a position to contradict them.
suggested_refs: The plain of Dura at Daniel 3:1, later attached to the dry-bones vision
sources: Later Jewish and Islamic folk tradition; not attested in any early source

stops.name: Tel Abib, the two sticks joined in his hand
stops.date_confidence: undated in the text; placed with the restoration oracles after the news of the fall
stops.campa: He takes one stick and writes on it, for Judah and the children of Israel his companions, and takes another and writes on it, for Joseph the stick of Ephraim and all the house of Israel his companions, and joins them one to another in his hand so that they become one. The northern kingdom has been gone for a hundred and thirty years and its people scattered by the Assyrians past any hope of a census. He holds them up in front of the exiles as one piece of wood, under one shepherd, in one land.
suggested_refs: The sign of the two sticks, Ezekiel 37:15-28

stops.name: Tel Abib, Gog of the land of Magog
stops.date_confidence: undated in the text; conventionally placed after the dry-bones vision on the order of the chapters
stops.campa: The last enemy in the book has no fixed address. Gog, of the land of Magog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, comes up from the uttermost parts of the north with Persia, Cush and Put, horses and horsemen all of them clothed with all sorts of armour, against a people gathered back out of the nations and dwelling safely in a land of unwalled villages. He falls upon the mountains of Israel, and the birds and the beasts are called to the sacrifice, and seven months are needed to bury the dead.
suggested_refs: Gog and Magog, Ezekiel 38-39, taken up in Revelation 20 and in Islamic tradition as Yajuj and Majuj

stops.name: The very high mountain, the man with the measuring reed
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day: the twenty-fifth year, the beginning of the year, tenth day, fourteen years after the city was smitten (Ezekiel 40:1), converting to about 28 April 573 BC. The mountain is not named in the text; the pin is set on the Temple Mount by convention
stops.campa: Twenty-five years into the exile and fourteen after the burning, the hand is on him again and he is brought in the visions of God into the land of Israel and set on a very high mountain, with the frame of a city on it. A man whose appearance is like brass stands in the gate with a line of flax and a measuring reed in his hand, and tells him to look and hear and set his heart on everything he is shown. Then they measure, gate by gate, chamber by chamber, in cubits so exact that Isaac Newton will one day rebuild the whole house on paper out of these numbers.
stops.quote: In the five and twentieth year of our captivity, in the beginning of the year, in the tenth day of the month, in the fourteenth year after that the city was smitten, in the selfsame day the hand of the Lord was upon me, and brought me thither.
suggested_refs: Isaac Newton's unpublished reconstruction of the Temple, worked out from the cubits of Ezekiel 40-42
sources: newton.journey.json (the Temple reconstruction from Ezekiel's cubits)

stops.name: The visionary house, the glory returns by the east gate
stops.date_confidence: attested; same vision unit as Ezekiel 40:1
stops.campa: He is brought to the gate that looks toward the east, and the glory of the God of Israel comes from the way of the east with a noise like the noise of many waters, and the earth shines with it. It is the same appearance he saw when he came to destroy the city and the same he saw by the river Chebar, and he falls on his face again. The glory goes into the house by the gate it left by, and the house is filled, and a voice from inside tells him this is the place of the soles of my feet, where I will dwell for ever.
suggested_refs: The sealed Golden Gate of the Temple Mount, read against Ezekiel 43:1-5 and 44:1-3

stops.name: The visionary house, the water from under the threshold
stops.date_confidence: attested; same vision unit as Ezekiel 40:1
stops.campa: Water comes out from under the threshold on the east side, south of the altar, and the man with the line leads him downstream measuring: a thousand cubits and the water is to the ankles, a thousand and it is to the knees, a thousand and it is to the loins, a thousand and it is a river he cannot pass over. On both banks stand trees whose leaf does not fade and whose fruit does not fail, new fruit every month, the leaf for medicine. The river runs down into the dead sea of that country and the waters are healed.
suggested_refs: The temple river of Ezekiel 47, taken up in Revelation 22 and in the Madaba map's Dead Sea

stops.name: The visionary city, the name of it from that day
stops.date_confidence: attested; same vision unit as Ezekiel 40:1
stops.campa: The land is divided in parallel strips from the great sea to the eastern border, a portion to each tribe, and a holy oblation in the middle for the sanctuary and the priests and the Levites, and a portion for the prince on either side of it. Strangers who sojourn among them and beget children are given an inheritance among the tribes they live in. The city has three gates on each side, twelve gates for the twelve tribes, and it is given a new name: the Lord is there. The book ends on the word there.
suggested_refs: YHWH Shammah, the closing name of Ezekiel 48:35

stops.name: Tel Abib, the last dated word
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day: the twenty-seventh year, first month, first day (Ezekiel 29:17), converting to about 26 April 571 BC. It is the latest of the roughly thirteen date formulas in the book, all reckoned from Jehoiachin's exile
stops.campa: Twenty-six years after the vision on the canal bank, he corrects himself in public. Nebuchadnezzar has served a great service against Tyre, every head made bald and every shoulder peeled, and got no wages out of it for himself or his army. So Egypt is given him instead, its multitude and its spoil and its prey, as pay for the work his army did. The oracle against Tyre delivered fifteen years earlier did not come out the way it was spoken, and the correction is written into the book beside it and left there.
suggested_refs: Ezekiel 29:17-21, the book's latest date and its own revision of Ezekiel 26

stops.name: Chaldea, the death that is not written
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction, and a gap. The Hebrew Bible records no death, no burial and no successor for Ezekiel; the book simply stops after 571 BC. The murder by a rebuked prince and the burial in a double cave in Chaldea come from the Lives of the Prophets, a Second Temple or early Christian era pseudepigraphon. The date is a convention, not a datum
stops.campa: After the twenty-seventh year the book gives no more dates and the prophet is not heard from again. Tradition, working long after and without documents, supplies what the canon leaves out: that a prince among the exiles whom he had rebuked for idolatry killed him, and that he was laid in a double cave on the Euphrates where Shem and Arpachshad were said to lie. He never sees the land he was carried through twice in vision. Judeans go home from this country in the next century; he does not.
suggested_refs: The Lives of the Prophets, the earliest account of Ezekiel's death and burial

stops.name: Al-Kifl, Benjamin of Tudela at the lamp that does not go out
stops.date_confidence: attested to Benjamin of Tudela's journey, reconstructed as to siting. Benjamin gives only a day's distance from Baghdad; the identification of that shrine with al-Kifl is a later fixing. Benjamin also reports that the exiled Jeconiah built the structure, a claim recorded centuries after the fact and not independently verifiable
stops.campa: Seventeen centuries after the prophet is buried, Benjamin of Tudela comes down the Euphrates a day out from Baghdad and finds the grave under sixty towers with a synagogue between every two of them, an ark in the court, the tomb behind it, and a lamp burning over it that is said never to have gone out. Jews come from Persia and Media at the New Year and the Day of Atonement, sixty to eighty thousand of them in the festival weeks by his count. In the vault they keep books said to be from the first house and the second.
suggested_refs: The Itinerary of Benjamin of Tudela, Adler translation, on the synagogue and tomb of Ezekiel
sources: Adler, The Itinerary of Benjamin of Tudela (1907)

stops.name: Al-Kifl, the dome raised over him in 1316
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year for the Ilkhanid work: the Al-Nukhailah mosque beside the tomb is dated to 1316 CE under Oljeitu, and 1316 is the earliest agreed date for elements of the standing structure. The tomb tradition itself is older, first mentioned in the tenth century by Sherira Gaon
stops.campa: The Ilkhanid ruler Oljeitu builds a mosque against the tomb and the shrine takes the shape it will keep: a conical dome on an octagonal drum with four windows, plaster ornament inside, Hebrew inscription on the walls of the chamber, and the tombs of other exiles and of custodian rabbis in the side rooms. In Islam he is Dhu al-Kifl, and the town takes its name from him. Two communities keep the same grave, each on its own calendar, in the same building, for six hundred years.
suggested_refs: The Al-Nukhailah mosque at al-Kifl, built 1316 under Oljeitu beside the tomb

stops.name: Al-Kifl, the last Passover of the Iraqi Jews
stops.date_confidence: attested to the period. Iraqi Jewish pilgrimage to al-Kifl, numbering over five thousand at Passover in the early twentieth century, ends with Operation Ezra and Nehemiah and the associated departures of 1950 to 1952. The restoration of the complex between 2010 and 2014 is separately documented; claims that Hebrew inscriptions were replaced with Quranic verses are not carried by that documentation and are left unverified here
stops.campa: Into the twentieth century more than five thousand Jews come out from Baghdad and Basra every Passover to the tomb on the Euphrates, light candles, leave votive offerings, and read from scrolls in a shrine their families have used for as long as their families have existed. Within two years of 1950 almost the whole community is gone from Iraq, airlifted out and stripped of its nationality. The pilgrimage that outlasted the Babylonian empire, the caliphates and the Ottomans ends inside a single generation.
suggested_refs: Operation Ezra and Nehemiah, 1950-1951, and the end of Jewish pilgrimage at al-Kifl
sources: general histories of the Iraqi Jewish exodus
